subject: Re: Redwood evals — next steps and dataset format
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@bancorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — Redwood evals next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- Goal: run a customer-specific evaluation to validate model fit for Bancorp's transaction-categorization and fraud-flagging prompts. You want accuracy/precision tradeoffs and a small set of recommended models for a POC (throughput: 20 qps, latency < 300ms p50).
- Scope: ~3k labelled examples initially (mix of short and long descriptions), binary fraud label + category. We recommend a stratified sample across product lines.
- Deliverables from Redwood: evaluation harness + leaderboard, recommended model variants (full/quantized), prompt-set suggestions, and an initial quality regression check against your baseline model.

Next steps:
1) You provide a sample dataset (CSV) with columns: id, input_text, expected_label. See format in the attached "bancorp-eval-promptset.csv".
2) Confirm scoring metric: precision@0.9 recall, and a confusion-matrix view. If you prefer F1 we can report both.
3) We'll spin up an eval runner on Redwood private infra (or hosted if you prefer) and share an initial leaderboard within 48 hours of dataset ingestion.

I'm attaching a short eval spec and the prompt set examples. Looping in Neha to coordinate the dataset ingestion and Rishi to scope any pricing/seat questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- bancorp-eval-promptset.csv (examples + prompt templates)
- bancorp-eval-specs.pdf (scoring rubric, infra, SLA)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@bancorp.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks — Redwood evals next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and exactly the kind of rigour we wanted. A couple quick clarifications before I pull the dataset together:

- On scoring: we care most about precision at a high threshold (we want to minimize false positives for fraud flags). Can you report precision@0.9 and overall micro-F1? Also include per-category precision/recall.
- On dataset format: will a single CSV be sufficient or do you need separate files for each product line? We can deliver a single file with a product_type column if that helps stratification.
- For the POC infra: we prefer Redwood hosted for speed, but if we hit any data residency concerns we may switch to Dedicated. Is there anything on our side to enable hosted evals?

I'll have a first 1k sample ready by Monday and can follow with the rest. Also please confirm whether you'll run evaluations against multiple model variants (e.g., 13B quantized, 70B base) so we can prioritize.

—Alex
Alex Johnson | Senior Product Manager, Fraud Ops
Bancorp
alex.johnson@bancorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@bancorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-11T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — Redwood evals next steps

Alex — great questions, answers inline below and a few operational notes:

1) Scoring: we'll report precision@0.90 (threshold-based), micro & macro F1, per-category precision/recall, and ROC-AUC for fraud detection. We'll also provide a confusion matrix and example failure cases for qualitative review.

2) Dataset format: single CSV is fine. Required columns: id, input_text, expected_label. Optional but recommended: product_type, created_at, severity. Please keep labels normalized (e.g., FRAUD_TRUE/FRAUD_FALSE or category names). Sample row provided in the CSV attachment.

3) Models to run: we suggest the following initial slate to cover cost/quality tradeoffs — we'll run them in parallel and produce a ranked leaderboard:
   - open-llm-13b-q4 (quantized) — low cost, faster inference
   - rwide-70b-base — higher quality, higher cost
   - redwood-rlhf-16b — tuned for classification/structured outputs

If you have a baseline model (your current in-house model or vendor), please include predictions as a separate column so we can compute regressions vs baseline. If not, we'll compute relative improvements vs the highest-performing Redwood run.

4) Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted is fine for the evals. For hosted we'll need a brief security attestation (we'll send a link to a short questionnaire) — no keys or PII should be uploaded without redaction. If there are residency limits we'll switch to a Dedicated runner.

Operational next steps: Neha will send you an ingestion guide and a Drive upload link; once we have the CSV we'll validate format and ingest. Rishi will follow up on any PO/contract questions if the evaluation expands beyond the POC scope.

Neha/Rishi — can you join a short intake call Tuesday to agree on the ingestion timeline and scoring thresholds? Alex — does 10am PT on Tuesday work?

Thanks,
Marissa

On attachments: see "bancorp-eval-promptset.csv" for the prompt templates we'll use during scoring.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood evals — intake call and dataset upload link

Alex — thanks and I'll take point on the data ingestion. Quick checklist and links:

- Upload link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/bancorp-evals (temporary, expires in 14 days)
- File requirements: CSV UTF-8; max 10MB per upload (we can stage multiple uploads). Columns: id, input_text, expected_label, product_type (optional), baseline_pred (optional).
- Scoring criteria (short): precision@0.9, micro-F1, per-category recall. We'll run both thresholded precision and top-K experiments if you want to evaluate confidence cutoffs.
- Redaction note: remove any raw PII (SSNs, full account numbers). If you need assistance with redaction we can provide a small script.

I'll schedule a 30-min intake at Tue 10:00 PT and send calendar invites. Once we validate the first upload I'll kick off the eval runner and share the leaderboard link (hosted) within 48 hours.

Attachments uploaded to the Drive include: bancorp-eval-specs.pdf (scoring rubric + infra) and bancorp-eval-promptset.csv.
